clue.text: Company taken in by cunning university official and cleric

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing, as in an arch look

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a dean is a senior official of a university faculty or college

explanation.surface: A cleric and a sly university official have a firm drawn into their dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' reads as companionship but is just its abbreviation; 'taken in by' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior Anglican clergyman ranking below a bishop, so he is a kind of cleric.

clue.text: Type of degree offered by topless roles

indicators.note: topless says the top letter of a down entry is removed

parts.note: parts are roles in a play

explanation.surface: A qualification earned by performing in topless roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter, P, from PARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Humanities qualifications such as a BA are degrees in this field.

clue.text: Local authority advice needing to be heard

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: counsel is advice or guidance

explanation.surface: A town hall's guidance demands an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing to be heard' gives a word sounding like COUNSEL, spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: An elected body running a town or district is its local government.

clue.text: Professional bridge-builder who might make an impression?

definitions.text: Professional bridge-builder who might make an impression?

parts.words: Professional bridge-builder who might make an impression?
parts.note: a bridge here is a false tooth anchored to its neighbours, and dentists take a mould, or impression, of the teeth

explanation.surface: A civil engineer leaving a mark on the landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a civil engineer; the bridge is dental work and the impression a mould of the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist who fits dental bridges and takes moulds of patients' teeth.

clue.text: Appointed in the role of token journalist

parts.note: as means in the capacity of, as in acting as chair
a sign is a token or indication
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is given the job of a figurehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Allocated to a post or task, the same sense as being appointed.

clue.text: Get the better of some, without doubt

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certainly beating a few rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition stopped at 'better', but the verb needs its object word: 'of' belongs to the definition, and 'some' alone points to letters lifted from 'without doubt'.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or beat someone is to get the better of them.

clue.text: One of the armed forces protected by American vessels

indicators.note: a thing protected by another is shielded within it, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: US is short for American, as in United States
RN is the Royal Navy, one of Britain's armed services

explanation.surface: A branch of the military guarded by American ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' in the surface suggests ships, but here it means containers; 'protected by' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Large vases or containers, such as for ashes or tea, are vessels.

clue.text: Poorly rated exercises in bureaucracy

indicators.note: poorly means badly done, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Workouts that score badly in an office system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' rearranges RATED into REDTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive official rules and paperwork are a byword for bureaucracy.

clue.text: Son shed tears before a team is dismissed

indicators.note: before says the pieces ahead of it come first in the answer

parts.note: wept means cried, shed tears
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A boy cried before his team was knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushed off or disregarded without consideration, which is what dismissed means.

clue.text: Article held in trust exceptionally for players out of form

indicators.note: something held in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
exceptionally suggests something done out of the ordinary way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammatical article kept in a trust for an unusual reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' makes TRUTS; 'held in' signals a container. A form is a school class, which truants skip.
explanation.definitionFit: Children who play truant are away from their school class, so they are players absent from form.

clue.text: Beginning to talk and walk like ducks? Nonsense!

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: ducks waddle, walking with a side-to-side sway

explanation.surface: Starting to chatter and walk like a duck? What rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to' takes T from 'talk'.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or trivial talk is rubbish, a common synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Sarah prepared father escargots, but very tough

indicators.note: prepared suggests ingredients made ready, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: da is an informal word for dad
escargots is the French culinary word for edible molluscs with shells

explanation.surface: Sarah cooked her dad a plate of escargots, which were rubbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges SARAH into ASHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for someone very hardy or unfeeling, extremely tough.

clue.text: Earth-shattering volte-face?

parts.note: shattering the word heart and putting its letters in a new order gives earth, so the clue word is the result of altering that organ

explanation.surface: A world-shaking reversal of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: alter the letters of HEART and you get EARTH, the clue's 'Earth-shattering'.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of opinion or policy, a sudden U-turn, which is what a volte-face is.

clue.text: Underwear with lace designed to be of limited size

parts.note: smalls is British slang for underwear

indicators.note: designed means reworked to a new plan, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lacy lingerie created in a modest size.
explanation.walkthrough: SMALLS is everyday British slang for underwear. 'designed' rearranges LACE into CALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest in extent or scope, describing something of limited size.

clue.text: Doctor misses treacle

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
misses are girls, also called lasses

explanation.surface: A doctor fails to take a dose of treacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses' looks like a verb but is a plural noun: young women.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark sweet syrup from sugar refining is what Americans call it; British treacle is the same thing.

clue.text: Constant smells from these inlets?

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant in maths, and for the speed of light
to reek is to smell strongly

explanation.surface: These coastal inlets give off a constant stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow water channels running into the coast or a river are small inlets.

clue.text: Do nothing in fixing train fare from India

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it
fixing means repairing or rearranging, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
O is the round figure for zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Idling while the railway gets mended, on a train journey in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' suggests a ticket price but means food. 'fixing' makes TANRI; 'in' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay-oven cooking is a style of Indian cuisine, food from that country.

clue.text: Desire must come before soldiers shine

indicators.note: one piece coming before another means it is placed first in the answer

parts.note: lust is strong desire
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British soldiers

explanation.surface: Passion has to precede the troops polishing their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle sheen or gloss on a surface is its shine.

clue.text: Afraid to cross river with evidence of injuries

indicators.note: to cross something is to stretch over it, so one piece spans the other, holding it inside

parts.note: scared means afraid

explanation.surface: Too fearful to ford a river, and bearing wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cross' puts SCARED around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked by healed wounds, which are evidence of past injuries.

clue.text: A clan involved in plot must be fair

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot, as in a flower bed

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A family caught up in a conspiracy needs to be even-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a conspiracy but is a garden bed. 'involved' makes ALANC; 'in' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Even-handed and impartial, weighing both sides, which is what a fair judgement is.

clue.text: Pad and copper ring used in climb

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: a piece used in another is placed inside it

parts.note: to shin up is to climb
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A mat and a copper loop for a climbing session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' puts O inside SHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft pad for sitting or kneeling on is a padded seat cover.

clue.text: His old gran? She lost these investments

indicators.note: letters that are lost are astray and out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grandmother laments having squandered her stock portfolio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges the letters of HIS OLD GRAN and SHE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakes owned in companies are a form of investment.

clue.text: Shellfish for me really encapsulates it!

indicators.note: encapsulates means holds inside, so the letters lie within the words

explanation.surface: An exclamation that this mollusc sums things up for the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encapsulates' finds the letters inside 'for me really'. An abalone found in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: An edible sea snail of the Channel Islands, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Responsibility, but it's our treat

definitions.meaning: a burden or duty that falls on someone
a phrase used when we pay the bill for others

explanation.surface: Footing the bill falls to us.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin word for burden, a duty or responsibility; split in two it is what a host says when paying.

clue.text: RADA, say, needs a friend with millions

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or companion
M is short for million

explanation.surface: A drama school needs a rich pal to fund it.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school, but here it is just an example of initials read as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed from initial letters, as RADA is, is an example of this term.

clue.text: Something that makes you cry about sanctimonious belief

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: chopping an onion makes the eyes water
pi is informal for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A tear-jerker about self-righteous conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is an informal short form of pious; 'about' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or judgement held by someone is their belief.

clue.text: Concludes dispatch moving leader to the Far East

indicators.text: moving leader to the Far East
indicators.note: the leading letter is moved to the far end, the east side of a word written across

parts.note: to send is to dispatch

explanation.surface: A news dispatch wraps up by relocating a chief to Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Far East' suggests Asia but just means the far end of the word: the first letter of SEND moves to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishes or brings to a close, the same verb sense as concludes.

clue.text: Racist son's cooked breakfast in France?

indicators.note: cooked suggests things altered or rigged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bigot's son makes a French morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges RACIST SONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaky crescent pastries are a classic French morning meal, hence the question mark for an example.
